decisions.summary: one link index per route: fabric_index(hard, WEB_HARD_GAP, walls, gap, water, 14.0) hoisted out of the string-pull
decisions.why: FR-002 as written. Verified against the code: _clear_link calls clear_runs(..., lines=water, tight=walls, tight_margin=gap) and clear_runs builds fabric_index(obstacles, margin, tight, tight_margin, lines, line_margin=14.0, cell=None) - the hoisted call is the same index, so the pull's verdicts and search are unchanged. Exact.

decisions.summary: the page from the structured blade and mark buckets, every other classed string parsed once and the parse handed to drop_offmap, merge_primitives, marks_region and hit_layer
decisions.why: FR-006 as written; byte identity is the proof. Note for the implementation: a marks slot is appended to a slot that may already hold crowns (flush_blade_groups), and a mark tuple carries its SVG snippet, so the struct must carry the slot's prefix string and read each mark's attributes once - that is still inside 'parse the rest once'. Magistracy pages also go through render_page (interactive/sheet.py), so they are among the pages that must come out byte-identical.

decisions.summary: the board's lazy caption test: seats sorted stably by (lab ok, score) descending, _sitable asked in that order, the first unshaded level-2 seat taken
decisions.why: FR-007 first half. Verified at siting.py:477-485: within _in_the_open every seat has the same (maximal) level, so max(key=(fits, lab ok, score)) is the first maximal (lab ok, score) seat, which a stable descending sort yields first; the shaded fallback and the no-level-2 case reduce to the old expression. Exact, provided board_caption_level stays side-effect free (the equality test covers it).

decisions.summary: the bamboo search outward: the old scan's positions sorted by (distance, scan index), first fit taken; the coarser sampling added only if SC-006's floor is missed
decisions.why: FR-008. Verified at bamboo.py: the old scan keeps the strictly nearest fit, first met on a tie, per scale - the sorted walk is the same seat if the positions are generated by the same float accumulation. The fallback is a MOVING change: if it is taken it must land after T09's identity proof, in the B phase, under SC-011's moving condition - not inside A4/T05 as the plan's placement suggests.

decisions.summary: _crosses_fabric box prefilters; _trim_to_service's field and steading tests and push_clear_of_fabric through RingIndex.edge_within; the comb's _dry through seg_reach_index
decisions.why: FR-009, all four named. Verified: edge_dist is the unsigned min seg_dist, so a polygon or edge whose box widened by gap misses the run segment's box can neither cross nor come within gap; push_clear_of_fabric's '>= gap' is exactly edge_within(...) is None; end_serves uses '<=' (closed) so the edge_within limit must admit equality, which the plan names and its at-the-bound tests cover; _dry's 'min seg_dist >= half' is the seg_reach_index test with extra 0. Exact.

decisions.summary: the grove draw's crown test through a CrownGrid of cells twice the largest crown radius
decisions.why: FR-011 (the grove draw). The predicate (woods.py:123) refuses only crowns within max(r, r_other); with a cell of at least 2x the largest radius ANY query or filed crown can have, the 3x3 cells hold every refusing crown and the same >= decides. The largest radius must be fixed before filing and cover the query radii (drawn grows as crowns land); the equality test should include a query larger than every filed crown.

decisions.summary: the toll's bitmap: set_crossing records the cells whose 3x3 neighborhood holds a sample; in_brook_band returns False at once outside it
decisions.why: FR-010. Exact: a point whose cell is not in the set would have found all nine lookups empty.

decisions.summary: the yards' mats: the floor test in arrays with a scalar band, the lattice counts as strided slice sums then the old order and _off_center tie-break, a box prefilter before _quad_gap
decisions.why: FR-011 and SC-009 (the mats byte-identical). Verified at yards.py: for a point inside a convex quad the boundary distance is the least distance to the edge lines, and the scalar band settles float edges; the old loop's final 'found' is the first candidate in iteration order with the greatest (count, -off-center), which the plan's walk of the max-count offsets in the old order reproduces if 'best count' is the global maximum; the box-gap prefilter is exact because a box separation is a lower bound on the quad gap. The floor quad must be convex (as _exact_lattice already assumes) - the recorded-yard equality test is the proof.

decisions.summary: A*: heap of (g + h, g, ix, iy), h = hypot(ix - gx, iy - gy) * cell
decisions.why: FR-001. The heuristic is admissible and consistent (a step costs hypot * cell plus a non-negative toll; the triangle inequality holds in lattice units), so the first pop of the goal is optimal on the lattice. The test is SC-002's.

decisions.summary: the coarser lattice: cells 12 and 14 tried; the largest with no more unreached houses than the base's taken
decisions.why: FR-003 raises the cell 'from 10 toward the width of the narrowest gap a way must thread (MIN_WEB_GAP)' - 18 ft in consts.py - and takes 'the largest cell under which' nothing is stranded, recording 'where it bites'. Stopping at 14 caps the search with no measurement: if 14 strands nothing, the plan neither tries 16 or 18 nor finds where it bites, and the request ('be willing to let things of that nature change if those changes would allow it to be significantly faster') is narrowed by an untested ceiling. Fix: step on toward MIN_WEB_GAP until a cell strands a house (or the gap width is reached), take the largest that does not, record every cell's counts. Two further clarifications the plan must state: (a) the cells raised are the 10-ft sites (the default and the explicit cell=10.0 calls), not the deliberately fine lattices (cell=5.0, 6.0, _FINE_CELL=3.0, sweeps' min(10, gap/6)), which FR-003 does not name; (b) 'none more than the base's' must be judged PER MAP and PER SEED (SC-011: 'no new or larger shortfall', 'no newly failing seed'), not as a total, and a stranding that the driver's re-roll hides (meta.roll_attempt rising) counts as a stranding.

decisions.summary: the field search carves at _predict_k after a short first guess; probes the top only when acreage grows less than SATURATION_GROWTH times the previous for a larger k
decisions.why: FR-004 as written, and the stubbed saturating/growing fan tests are SC-003's. SATURATION_GROWTH is a new magic number and needs its why recorded beside it.

decisions.summary: the carve's rows as arrays: bounds, interpolation, wobble and drift in numpy over the columns, the supply push per vertex scalar through the memo, then the quad tests
decisions.why: FR-005 names three things as array operations: 'each sector's row-by-column bund vertices AND THEIR PUSHES OFF THE SUPPLY BANKS, AND THE PLOT TESTS, as numpy arrays'. The plan keeps the push (_clear_supply in carve.py's edge) scalar and leaves the quad tests (spills, above, in_supply) as they are, with no stated reason. It is purpose-fatal because FR-005 is judged by wall time and withdrawn if it does not pay: a lever implemented without its costliest parts can fail that test and be recorded as 'tried and withdrawn', which records the GM's table item as not paying when the form the spec describes was never tried. Fix: vectorize the push and the plot tests as FR-005 says, or, if a part genuinely cannot be vectorized, bring that as a MODE 1 exception with the measurement.

decisions.summary: the board's candidates every 24 px along a route instead of 12, for hamlets and villages, kept only if the notice stage is faster
decisions.why: FR-007 does not tier-scope the coarsening, so leaving towns and cities at 12 px narrows it. It stands: the only callers outside the hamlet/village tiers are the frozen legacy town maps, which never regenerate, so nothing that rolls is exempted and the request's purpose (the pool rolling faster) loses nothing; and FR-007's own statement of the change's effect ('a few feet along its verge') holds only at the hamlet/village grain - at 3 ft/px the same step is 36 ft. Clarify in the plan whether stage_notice's frame re-seat (hamletgen/frame.py:263, its own 12 px lattice along a route) moves to 24 as well; the notice bucket counts it.

decisions.summary: landing order: A lands, the pool regenerates byte-identical against 5f15c65bd, then B
decisions.why: The order is right (SC-011: the exact changes shown byte-identical before the moving ones land), but the reference is wrong: since 5f15c65bd main has merged 283 (be67a7e97, ce7db300f), which changes interactive/compound_kinds and the ochiba and ubame magistracy SVGs, and magistracy pages go through render_page, which A2 changes. Compared against 5f15c65bd, T09 will show differences A did not cause. The reference must be the commit A lands on (the clone's HEAD just before the first A commit, and again after any main merge during A), regenerated in a detached worktree at that commit.

decisions.summary: the grove fill, the seam closing, the commons and the flush re-profiled after A, each given its lever; the after-profile read under the same rule
decisions.why: FR-011 and SC-009 allow 'or the plan's measurement says why no allowed change reaches it'; deferring the choice of lever to a re-profile is within. A lever here that moves a map is held to SC-011's moving condition (T16 follows T15, so it is).
